plan.title: EOL-normalize ownership detection and restore narrow LF gitattributes for managed paths

narratives.Description: On Windows with core.autocrlf=true, checkout CRLF makes Directive-managed files look user-owned. Setup refuses overwrite, drops ownership entries, and never writes wiring-ready, so clone-and-go fails AC14.10/AC8.6.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Update packages/runtime/src/ownership-fix.ts so ownership/wrapper fingerprint comparison EOL-normalizes before equality, treating CRLF-versus-LF-only diffs as Directive-managed rather than user content.
2. Restore narrow LF .gitattributes deposit for managed paths in packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts and packages/runtime/src/setup-wiring.ts (prior 0.126 behavior), and extend ownership-fix.test.ts plus scaffold.test.ts fixtures to assert EOL-normalized compare and LF attribute deposit.
narratives.UserStory: As a Windows consumer cloning an OVPR repo with default autocrlf, I want first eligible command to finish local wiring, so that doctor can go in sync without false user-content conflicts.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a managed file differs from the expected bytes only by CRLF versus LF, when ownership/wrapper detection runs, then it treats the file as Directive-managed rather than user content.
Given setup/repair deposits managed-path attributes, when .gitattributes is written, then managed paths are pinned to LF without a broad repo-wide eol rewrite.

expected_outputs: ownership-fix and scaffold tests pass for EOL-normalized compare and LF attributes
